in_hindi.long_meaning: अम्मान एक ऐसा नाम है जो शांति और सुरक्षा की भावना को दर्शाता है। यह नाम अक्सर एक सुरक्षित और शांतिपूर्ण स्थान या समुदाय के संदर्भ में उपयोग किया जाता है। यह नाम माता-पिता द्वारा अपने बच्चे के लिए एक सुरक्षित और शांतिपूर्ण भविष्य की कामना के रूप में चुना जा सकता है।

in_pashto.name: امان
in_pashto.long_meaning: امان دى يو نوم چې د امن او ارام احساس څرګندوي. دا نوم ډیری وخت داسې ځای یا ټولنې په حواله کارول کیږي چیرته چې خلک خوندي او راضي احساس کوي.

in_english.name: Amman
in_english.meaning: A place or community of peace and safety
in_english.long_meaning: The name Amman is derived from the Arabic root 'أمّان' (Ammān), which signifies a place or community where people feel safe and secure. This name reflects the values of peace, tranquility, and protection. In Islamic tradition, the concept of Amman is associated with the idea of a haven or refuge. The name is not directly mentioned in the Quran but is related to the Arabic concept of 'aman' (أمان), which means peace or safety. The name Amman is used across various Muslim cultures to signify a place of solace and security.

data.cultural_impact: Amman, the capital city of Jordan, boasts a rich history that spans over 7,000 years. The name "Amman" may have come from the Ammonites, an ancient civilization that inhabited the region around 4000 BCE. The name "Al-Madinah Al-Mulqaddasah," meaning "the noble city," suggests the significance of this ancient city in Arab and Islamic culture. It is considered a center of commerce and politics, as well as being a melting pot of various influences from Roman and Greek to Persian and Arabic. The vibrant Amman of today showcases a unique fusion of modernity and tradition, offering tourists and residents alike a wealth of historical, cultural, and trade opportunities.
data.spiritual_significance: Amman, in its Islamic context, carries a profound spiritual significance beyond being just a historical and cultural site. To many Muslims, the name represents a sacred connection to Allah as embodied in the phrase "the high place of Allah." It can serve as a reminder of the importance of sacred spaces in the Islamic faith, where individuals can seek solace, worship, and connect with the divine. The spiritual significance also extends to the idea of a community, or ummah, that gathers together to build a city, or madinah, that continues to grow and thrive under the divine protection of Allah. This spiritual concept is represented by the multiple mosques and religious sites that are spread across Amman, attracting pilgrims from all corners of the world.
